claims.text: Every given pure SPE has an exact-payoff-equivalent pure SPE with n*3^n vertex-update states on all set-sized arbitrary-branching arenas; after all legal histories.
Unconditional pure finite-memory SPE existence follows from the old lower-semicontinuous-payoff theorem.
For every k>=1 every E-winning SPE in the constructed degree-two O(k^2) family requires binomial(k,floor(k/2)) states, at least 2^k/(k+1).
Main posed the arena-independent constrained-SPE memory question.
Full-version Proposition 9 equates Reach weak SPE and SPE; Proposition 19/Corollary 21 give finite-arena reconstruction; Theorem 34 already gives FPT.
Author-postprint Theorem 7 uses leaf outcomes and outcome-indexed positional paths under absorbing-leaf hypotheses; Theorem 16 gives finite-range weak-SPE existence.
Author-version Theorem 23 gives quadratic player-dependent NE memory; Remark 1 distinguishes vertex and edge memory.
Flesch et al. Section 3.3 uses payoff-minimizing continuations after deviations.
Alluwaym et al. gives stationary randomized SPEs on finite graphs and a pure absorbing-target special case.
Exponential SPE memory and checking constructions have prior antecedents; generalized reachability uses subset memory.
Flesch Theorem 2.3 permits arbitrary action sets, history-dependent actions, pure strategies and prefix-retaining subgame payoffs.
Exact finite checks verified 2827 SPE inputs and recompressions and k=1,...,6 lower families; omission controls failed.
The comparison is bounded; no effective arbitrary-infinite-arena algorithm, new FPT result, broad-objective extension or optimal base is proved.
